name: GRAND
aliases: Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection

intervals.label: proposed
intervals.quote: planned large-scale observatory: 20 separate, independent sub-arrays, each of 10,000 radio antennas deployed over 10,000 km^2
intervals.note: Start is the 2018 white paper's submission date; the full 200,000-antenna GRAND array remains at the proposal stage as of the most recent prototype paper fetched (2026).

intervals.label: GRANDProto300 13-antenna stage (GP300_s13)
intervals.quote: In June 2023, the deployment of the 13-antenna stage, GP300_s13, was completed.
intervals.note: 13-antenna configuration operated for nearly two years before being extended/decommissioned in April 2025; this is a prototype/pathfinder stage of the GRAND programme, not the full array.

intervals.label: GRANDProto300 65-antenna stage (GP300_s65)
intervals.quote: By April 2025, the array was extended to its current 65-antenna stage (GP300_s65), built south of GP13, covering an area of about 30 km².
intervals.note: Prototype/pathfinder stage; the design GRANDProto300 target is 300 antennas over 200 km².

physics_goals.value: Detect ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrinos and cosmic rays using giant radio antenna arrays sensitive to air showers and Earth-skimming neutrino-induced showers
physics_goals.quote: planned large-scale observatory: 20 separate, independent sub-arrays, each of 10,000 radio antennas deployed over 10,000 km^2, for a total of 200,000 antennas

quantity.quote: the array was extended to its current 65-antenna stage (GP300_s65)
quantity.note: Prototype stage, not the full design array.

quantity.quote: 20 separate, independent sub-arrays, each of 10,000 radio antennas deployed over 10,000 km^2, for a total of 200,000 antennas

notes: No site record was created for GRAND: GRANDProto300 is located, per its collaboration's own progress paper, '200 km^2 in the Gobi Desert near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China', but no fetched source states a numeric latitude/longitude. Per A17, a coordinate was not invented; detector:grand's placements are left empty with the same note.

Three small-scale prototype arrays exist since 2023 per the 2026 JINST paper: GRAND@Nancay (France), GRAND@Auger (Argentina) and GRANDProto300 (China); only GRANDProto300 is modelled in any detail here since it is the collaboration's own most-covered prototype in the sources fetched.
No INSPIRE experiment-registry lookup was performed for GRAND in this session; external.inspire_experiment left null.
Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

summary.plain: A proposed giant array of 200,000 radio antennas spread over a huge area, designed to catch the radio flash from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and neutrinos. Small test versions are already running in China, France and Argentina.
summary.technical: Proposed 200,000-antenna, 20-sub-array giant radio observatory for ultra-high-energy neutrinos and cosmic rays. Full array remains at proposal stage; the GRANDProto300 prototype in the Gobi Desert near Dunhuang, China grew from a 13-antenna stage (deployed June 2023) to a 65-antenna stage (April 2025), alongside sister prototypes GRAND@Nancay (France) and GRAND@Auger (Argentina), all operating since 2023.
